uncited: It differs from [AABB Culling](1789-aabb-culling.md) by testing mutual containment (box inside frustum AND frustum inside box) rather than just box outside frustum, and from [Bounding Box Culling](1806-bounding-box-culling.md) by operating on explicit frustum planes rather than generic bounding volumes.
- Input: A 4x4 projection-view matrix $M$ (column-major), and an AABB defined by minimum corner $(x_l, y_l, z_l)$ and maximum corner $(x_h, y_h, z_h)$.
The normal $(n_x, n_y, n_z)$ is normalized.
- `Frustum`: Contains an array of 6 `Plane` objects and an array of 8 `vec4` points representing the frustum corners in world space.
**Extract Frustum Planes:** Compute the 6 planes from the matrix $M$.
**Test Box Against Planes:** For each of the 6 planes, determine if all 8 corners of the box lie behind the plane.
A corner $C_j$ is behind the plane if $P \cdot C_j < 0.0$.
**Test Frustum Against Box:** Compute the 8 corners of the frustum in world space (using the inverse projection-view matrix).
For each axis ($x, y, z$), check if all 8 frustum corners lie outside the box on the same side (i.e., all $> \text{box}_{\text{max}}$ or all $< \text{box}_{\text{min}}$).
- **Degenerate Input:** If the projection matrix results in a zero-length normal for a plane, normalization fails.
- **Boundary Conditions:** The test returns `true` if the box touches the frustum boundary (not strictly outside).
- **Time Complexity:** Constant time $O(1)$, involving a fixed number of arithmetic operations (6 plane extractions, 6 plane tests with 8 corners each, 3 axis tests with 8 corners each).
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(1)$ auxiliary space for plane and corner calculations.
- **Strengths:** Robust for large bounding boxes where simple view frustum culling might fail due to the box spanning the camera or extending far into the distance.
- **Limitations:** Requires computing frustum corners in world space for the second part of the test, which involves matrix inversion.
- **When to use:** When culling volume rendering geometry that may be large or distant, ensuring no part of the box is missed by the view frustum.

It addresses the limitation of standard frustum culling which only checks if the box is outside the frustum, failing when the box is large enough to encompass the camera or extend beyond the frustum boundaries in complex ways.
